subject: Physical Education
name: Basic 4 Physical Education
description: The Basic 4 Physical Education curriculum focuses on refining motor skills, understanding movement concepts, developing physical fitness, and cultivating positive values. It includes advanced locomotor and manipulative skills, rhythmic activities, strategies for game situations, fitness assessment, and knowledge of health and safety in physical activities.

strands.title: MOTOR SKILL AND MOVEMENT PATTERNS
strands.description: Developing competence in motor skills and movement patterns for various physical activities.

subStrands.title: LOCOMOTOR, MANIPULATIVE AND RHYTHMIC SKILLS
subStrands.description: Developing advanced locomotor, manipulative and rhythmic skills.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate competence in the motor skills and movement patterns needed to perform a variety of physical activities (games, athletics gymnastics and dance)

indicators.description: Demonstrate the difference between slow and fast, heavy and light, hard and soft while moving.

exemplars.description: Learners demonstrate slow and fast movements. Learners move in a demarcated area using varied locomotor skills (walk, jog and run).
Learners walk or run for peers to determine slow or fast movement.

indicators.description: Enter, jump, and leave a long swinging rope turned by others repeatedly.

exemplars.description: Learners skip a number of times at their own pace landing on the balls of their feet. Skip continuously over a rope a number of times in turns.

indicators.description: Roll ball with a stick to a target.

exemplars.description: Learner rolls a balls with their sticks to a distance after general and specific warm-up. Learner practice ball rolling in varied patterns such as straight rolling, curve rolling, etc.

indicators.description: Perform an inverted balance (tripod) by evenly distributing weight on body parts.

exemplars.description: Learners perform headstand with hands supporting. Learners with difficulty are supported by peers.

indicators.description: Balance while moving and manipulating objects on a ground-level balance beam.

exemplars.description: After a warm-up, learners pick rubber balls available hold with their two hands and raise them at a stationery position. Let them lift the balls over their head and begin to walk while maintaining a balance.

indicators.description: Strike a bounce ball with the hands and feet.

exemplars.description: In pairs, a partner tosses a lightweight ball to a colleague to hit over varying distances. Serve a lightweight ball to a partner, using the underhand movement pattern. Strike a gently tossed ball with feet, using a side orientation.

indicators.description: Strike a self-tossed light weight ball with a paddle or racket to a partner.

exemplars.description: In pairs, a partner tosses a lightweight ball to a colleague to hit over varying distances. Serve a lightweight ball to a partner, using the underhand movement pattern. Strike a gently tossed ball with a bat, using a side orientation.

indicators.description: Throw a flying disc for distance using the backhand movement pattern.

exemplars.description: Throw a tennis ball to a partner over a distance using the overhand throw technique. Throw a flying disc (Frisbee disc) for distance, using the backhand movement pattern. Let them perform in turns to acquire the right skill.

indicators.description: Show the difference in throwing to a stationary and a moving partner.

exemplars.description: After a general and specific warm up, put a container or basket at a point. Learners with objects to use different techniques to throw the object into to container or object.
Learners identify the best technique the gives them accuracy and precision.
Organise coopetition in groups.

indicators.description: Catch a ball above the head and near the middle of the body while jogging and running.

exemplars.description: After general and specific warm up, learners catch balls thrown above from distance in the air with the hand. Vary the distance and let them do for fun. Accuracy must be considered.

indicators.description: Kick a ball dropped from the hands.

exemplars.description: Learners control a ball dropped by their pairs. They should control them from a 15-metre distance on the ground with the foot. Put them into groups to control their ball.

indicators.description: Keep a hand-dribbled ball away from a defensive partner.

exemplars.description: Learners in pairs after a warm up. They use their hands to dribble balls away from their partners. Learners alternate the hand used in the dribble. Keep ball away from partners by placing your body in between ball and partner.

indicators.description: Keep a foot-dribbled ball away from a defensive partner.

exemplars.description: In pairs, footdribble -a ball away from partner. Alternate the foot used in the dribble. Learners keep balls away from partner by placing your body in between ball and partner.

indicators.description: Dance to the beat of traditional music.

exemplars.description: Learners dance to a beat of any traditional music. Learners dance as individually but at their own pace.

indicators.description: Perform movement skill with one hand or one foot and compare with movement skill with two hands and two feet.

exemplars.description: Learners perform movement skills with one hand or foot and compared with performing movement skills with two hands and two feet.

indicators.description: Roll smoothly in a backward direction (back roll).

exemplars.description: Learners demonstrate how to roll backwards. Learners in pair by supporting each other to bend backwards smoothly. Learners must be guided to avoid injuries. Those who can roll backwards on their own, should be granted the opportunity to demonstrate to their peers.

strands.title: MOVEMENT CONCEPTS, PRINCIPLES AND STRATEGIES
strands.description: Understanding movement concepts, principles, and strategies.

subStrands.title: SPACE AWARENESS, DYNAMICS, RELATIONS, BODY MANAGEMENT AND STRATEGIES
subStrands.description: Understanding space, dynamics, and body management.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge of movement concepts, principles, and strategies that apply to the learning and performance of physical activities.

indicators.description: Distinguish between self-space and open space.

exemplars.description: Learners explain the difference between self-space and open space through discussion.
Learners also use indicate self- space and open space by ticking the spaces provides on a sheet appropriately.

indicators.description: Explain the difference between throwing to a stationary partner and throwing to a moving partner.

exemplars.description: Hold ball in the left hand. Place the left foot slightly forward in front of the body. Bend body slightly over the ball, pick a target, and swing the free right hand backward to contact the lower middle part of the ball (for right handed learners). When the partner is moving, the thrower would have to intensify the throw.

indicators.description: Identify body parts that are used for kicking a ball.

exemplars.description: Learner identify body parts that can be used in kicking a ball as hands. Learners stand with their legs opened and move to a ready position to kick a ball.

indicators.description: Describe the appropriate body orientation to serve a ball, using the underhand movement pattern.

exemplars.description: Learner stands with feet shoulder width apart. Learner tosses the ball and swings the hand forward to strike the ball upward and forward. Learner moves the hind leg forward to recover.
Learners practice with feedback as individual and in a group for mastery, Learners progress at their own pace.

indicators.description: Identify the difference between dribbling a ball (with the hand and the foot, separately) while moving forward and when changing direction.

exemplars.description: Dribbling is the act of keeping the ball under the control of the player with the ball. In dribbling without opponent, the player with the ball is under no pressure and at liberty to do whatever he/she wants to do with the ball within the rules of the game. When dribbling with an opponent, the player with the ball is being contested for the ball and as a result has to consider the movements and actions of the opponent as well as keep the ball under control away from the opponent.

subStrands.title: AEROBIC CAPACITY, STRENGTH, ENDURANCE AND FLEXIBILITY

contentStandards.description: Assess and maintain a level of physical fitness to improve health and performance.

indicators.description: Perform 15 minutes' brisk walk with music.

exemplars.description: Learners warm-up to begin activities. Learners swing their arms by walking briskly within a demarcated area at their own pace.

indicators.description: Perform continuous 'v' push-up

exemplars.description: Learner demonstrates the correct position by sitting on the floor, straightening the legs and open to 'v' shape and keep palms flat on the floor. Learners lift the body up at their own pace.

indicators.description: Perform two sets of eight continuous 'v' push-ups.

exemplars.description: Learner demonstrates the correct position by sitting on the floor, straightening the legs and open to 'v' shape and keep palms flat on the floor by learners and try to lift the body up for continuously three set with 4 mins' rest after each set.

indicators.description: Perform groin flexibility

exemplars.description: Learners in pairs facing each other. The one working uses the other as a support with one hand while standing on one foot. Learner flexes the free leg and use the other hand to the ankle and pull it backward. Learners can also do the exercise using a wall or any firm support.

indicators.description: Identify body types such as endomorph (big body), mesomorph (medium body) and ectomorph (slim Body)

exemplars.description: Learners identify the three body types as endomorph, mesomorph and ectomorph

strands.title: PHYSICAL FITNESS CONCEPTS, PRINCIPLES AND STRATEGIES
strands.description: Understanding fitness concepts for health and performance.

subStrands.title: FITNESS PROGRAMME, HEALTHY DIET, SAFETY AND INJURIES, SUBSTANCES/DRUGS AND BODY COMPOSITION
subStrands.description: Concepts related to fitness, health, and safety.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge of physical fitness concepts, principles, and strategies to improve health and performance

indicators.description: Identify the heart rate intensity (target heart-rate range) that is necessary to increase aerobic capacity.

exemplars.description: Learners walk, power walk, walk-jog, jog at their own pace keeping the heart rate at maximum aerobic endurance level (70-75%) at least three times a week. Incorporate aerobic dance and circuit training and strength training in this moderate to vigorous physical activity.

indicators.description: Discuss how prolong physical activity increases endurance, allowing movement to occur for longer periods of time.

exemplars.description: Learners discuss how prolong activities like jogging, walking, etc. improve endurance.

indicators.description: Explain how the intensity and duration of exercise, as well as nutritional choices, affect energy use during physical activity.

exemplars.description: Learners discuss the relationship between intensity and duration of exercises. The higher the intensity, the shorter should be the duration. In high intensity activity, the body burns nutrients faster and requires more nutrient intake at the end of the activity to maintain equilibrium.

indicators.description: Identify muscles being strengthened during the performance of particular physical activities.

exemplars.description: Push-ups strengthen the biceps muscles and muscles of the chest. Chin-ups strengthen the triceps muscle. Step-ups strengthen both the hamstrings and the quadriceps (muscles of the thigh).

indicators.description: Classify PE equipment under safe and unsafe.

exemplars.description: Assemble a variety of sports equipment, both old and new for learners to classify them into safe and unsafe.

indicators.description: Identify the effects of drugs use for physical activities.

exemplars.description: Learners discuss the short-term and long-term effects of drugs. The effects can be physical and psychological. Advice learners not to involve themselves in drugs. Let them know some of the dangers like sleepless night, loss of appetite, blood pressure, body temperature, panic, seizure, rashes etc.

strands.title: VALUES AND PSYCHO-SOCIAL CONCEPTS, PRINCIPLES AND STRATEGIES
strands.description: Developing values and social skills through physical activity.

subStrands.title: SELF-RESPONSIBILITY, SOCIAL INTERACTION, GROUP DYNAMICS AND CRITICAL THINKING
subStrands.description: Values, social interaction, and critical thinking.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate value and utilize knowledge of psychological and sociological concepts, principles, and strategies that apply to the learning and performance of physical activity

indicators.description: Accept responsibility for one's own behaviour in a group activity.

exemplars.description: Obey rules and regulations for the activity. Appreciate and accept calls from officiating officials. Learners must be responsible for their own actions.

indicators.description: Participate in a variety of group settings (e.g., partners, small groups and large groups) without interfering with others.

exemplars.description: Encourage learners to work in groups and observe group dynamics such as tolerance, self-respect, teamwork, etc.

indicators.description: Demonstrate respect for self, others, and equipment during physical activities.

exemplars.description: Learners observe the rules for self-integrity.
Learners respect peer and others when working together
Learners use equipment for what they were made for as well as respect their use with peers.

indicators.description: Distinguish between acts of physical courage and physically reckless acts and explain the key characteristics of each.

exemplars.description: Learners identify the difference between physical courage as taking action but care and physically reckless as taking action without care. The former has the key characteristics of observing the rules of the game or sports.
